page.text:
A foundational technique in abstract algebra is the synthesis of complex
systems from elementary components. The *direct product* $G_1 \times G_2$
of two groups constructs a new group whose carrier set is the Cartesian
product of the underlying sets, with the group operation evaluated
independently in each coordinate.

Categorically, the direct product constitutes the categorical product in
the category $\mathbf{Grp}$: it is equipped with canonical projection
homomorphisms $\pi_1 : G_1 \times G_2 \to G_1$ and
$\pi_2 : G_1 \times G_2 \to G_2$ such that for any group $H$ and pair of
homomorphisms $f_1 : H \to G_1, f_2 : H \to G_2$, there exists a unique
homomorphism $f : H \to G_1 \times G_2$ satisfying $\pi_i \circ f = f_i$.
